You may not ban the Tiebreaker.\n   2. Ban Order: ABBAAB (Team 1 Bans, Team 2 Bans, Team 2 Bans, Team 1 Bans, Team 1 Bans, Team 2 Bans).\n```\n\n**Copy this into Cell A4:**\n```text\n4. Other mods outside the “Difficulty Reduction” and “Difficulty Increase” category are NOT allowed.\n```\n\n**Copy this into Cell A5:**\n```text\n5. Disconnects, technical difficulties \u0026 Tiebreakers\n   1. If a player disconnects in the first 30 seconds of a map, the map can be aborted and replayed once. If they disconnect later again, their score counts from the moment they disconnect.\n   2. If the match score reaches 6-6, the teams will play the Tiebreaker (TB). The TB is played as FreeMod, but mods are strictly optional for all players.\n```\n\n**Copy this into Cell A6:**\n```text\n6. Custom rulesets:\n   1.       "text": "**Analyzing Tournament Ruleset**\n\nI\u0027m currently focused on the user\u0027s objective: to get feedback on an osu! tournament ruleset. I\u0027ve identified key terms and I\u0027m analyzing how these relate to potential problems or areas for discussion.\n\n\n**Reviewing Tournament Pool**\n\nI\u0027m now diving deeper into the ruleset\u0027s components. The pool setup appears standard for a late-stage tournament. The lobby mechanics are also conventional, though I\u0027m noting the team vs team structure, as it warrants further examination concerning the \"FreeMod\" stipulations. The roll/protect system seems atypical, but manageable. I\u0027m especially focused on the FreeMod rules; they sound a bit ambiguous.\n\n\n**Clarifying FreeMod Mechanics**\n\nI\u0027m now zeroing in on the FreeMod (FM) rules, which seem to introduce significant strategic complications in this 2v2 tournament structure. I\u0027m concerned that requiring teams to \"match\" or \"exceed\" mod choices fundamentally alters FM. This potentially transforms strategy into a \"chicken\" match of mod-countering. I\u0027m also finding the mod hierarchy particularly perplexing and the ambiguity of the *match* requirement creates several logical conflicts. I\u0027m considering all possibilities.\n\n\n**Questioning Mod Matching**\n\nI\u0027m now deeply concerned about the FreeMod stipulation. I\u0027m wondering what \"match\" means in terms of Team B\u0027s response to Team A\u0027s mod choices. Is it a sum, or does each player need to match individually? This rule demands clarification. The disconnect and tiebreaker rules are standard, and the osu!lazer-specific rules, such as EZ adjustment, are welcome.\n\n\n**Addressing Mod Choice Ambiguity**\n\nI\u0027m now honing in on the crucial FreeMod ambiguity. Specifically, I\u0027m questioning if \"match\" requires individual players to duplicate mod choices, as that would essentially lead to mod-based strategic lockouts. It raises many further concerns if one team takes FL+HD+HR, and the other can\u0027t, for example. The FM rules would effectively work as a ban/cheese phase, which is contrary to the intent of FreeMod. My recommendation is to revert to standard FM rules. I\u0027ve also identified inconsistencies regarding Team Size in the rules. It could be far more clear!\n\n\n**Evaluating Mod Scoring**\n\nI\u0027m now focused on the finer points of the FreeMod rules. I\u0027m concerned about the proposed EZ buff, as equating it to HDHR for matching feels odd. The rules don\u0027t explain how one can \"match\" a \"BL\" mod at all. A points system or clear table would be necessary if the rule stands. I\u0027ve also identified a point about the Pick/Protect order that needs double-checking. The Lazer-specific rules, especially the EZ score adjustment, are praised.",

      "text": "\n\n\nOverall, this is a very well-structured ruleset that clearly takes advantage of the new features in **osu!lazer** (Difficulty Adjust, EZ multiplier, Lazer API, Blinds/Cover mods). Most of the rules for match flow, bans, and disconnects are industry-standard and solid.\n\nHowever, there is **one major red flag** in the FreeMod section that could cause a lot of arguments, especially since you mentioned matches can be \"self-refereed.\" \n\nHere is a breakdown of what is good, what needs fixing, and what you should clarify:\n\n### 🚨 The Major Issue: The FreeMod \"Matching\" Rule (Rule 4.3)\n**Rule 4.3.2 says:** *\"The opposing team (of the pick) MUST match the mods of the picking team, with equivalent or harder mods.\"*\n\nThis is highly unusual for osu! tournaments and is going to cause massive headaches. \n* **It allows for \"Cheese\" strategies:** If Team A picks an FM map and both players pick Flashlight (FL), Team B is now *forced* to play FL. This completely defeats the purpose of FreeMod, which is usually to allow players to play to their individual mod strengths. Instead, it turns FM into a \"counter-pick and force the enemy to fail\" pool.\n* **It is too ambiguous for self-reffing:** How exactly do players \"match\"? If Team A has Player 1 on HD and Player 2 on EZ. Does Team B have to mirror them exactly? Or can Team B put Player 1 on EZ and Player 2 on HD? What if Team A takes HD+HR on one player, and NM on the other? \n* **My Recommendation:** Ditch the \"matching\" rule entirely. Use the standard osu! FreeMod rule: *\"On FreeMod picks, at least ONE player per team must take a difficulty-increasing mod (HD, HR, FL, etc.) or EZ.\"* If you want everyone to play mods, you can say: *\"On FreeMod picks, ALL players must take at least one mod.\"* Let teams pick the mods they are comfortable with.\n\n### ⚠️ Minor Clarifications Needed\n* **What is the Team Size?** Rule 1.1 says \"(Team) vs (Team)\", but Rule 4.3.1 says \"**BOTH** team players\". This implies the tournament is a 2v2 format. If it is 2v2, you should explicitly state that in Rule 1.1 (e.g., `Format: 2v2 Team vs Team`). \n* **The Protect Order:** Rule 2.4 says \"The team that picks first protects first.\" This is fine, but be aware of the strategy it creates. If Team A wins the roll, they have to calculate: *\"If I choose First Pick, I also have to Protect first, which lets Team B counter-protect.\"* Usually, tournaments make the *Second* Pick protect first to balance the advantage of getting the first map pick.\n* **Mod Hierarchy (4.3.4):** You wrote `EZ \u003d HDHR`. While Lazer allows you to adjust the EZ multiplier to 1.0x (making it not ruin your score), EZ and HDHR are fundamentally completely different skill sets.
